rules.condition: requester drives APB transfers to the bridge (assumption ASM-001)
rules.statement: The APB requester must issue one Setup phase then Access until PREADY, keep fields stable, and keep PSTRB low in a read.

rules.condition: PWAKEUP is used by a clock controller and a request is in flight
rules.statement: The clock controller using PWAKEUP must keep i_clk_slv running while a request is in flight, since the bridge cannot detect a request on a stopped clock.
The bridge architecture must be a request/acknowledge handshake with bundled data held stable, not an asynchronous FIFO.
One parameter selects APB4 or APB5; APB5 adds PWAKEUP and user signals with configurable widths; no parity check signals are provided.
ADDR_W defaults to 32 (range 1 to 32), DATA_W defaults to 32 (8, 16 or 32), PSTRB and PPROT are always present, and user widths default to 0.
Every APB output must be a flip-flop output; PREADY must be high only in state RESP, i.e. only once the Access phase has been reached.
The response must be delivered only after the handshake has closed (acknowledge low), so the next Setup phase can always be accepted.
The RTL top must declare the APB5 ports in every configuration, with user widths of at least 1, unused inputs ignored and unused outputs 0.
